lead.headline: Indian startup funding falls 47.5% in October as no deal reaches $100 million
lead.hook: Indian startups raised ==$678 million in October, down 47.5% from September's $1.29 billion==, because no single round reached $100 million.
points: Year on year the drop is steeper: 60.8%, from $1.73 billion in October 2025. February and June 2026 were the strongest months, at about $2 billion each.

Only Tessolve ($75 million, semiconductor solutions) and Even Healthcare ($50 million) crossed $50 million. Growth and late-stage deals totalled $414.6 million across 20 rounds; early-stage deals $263 million across 79.
Bengaluru took $420 million across 52 deals, 61.97% of the total. Delhi-NCR got $110.26 million and Mumbai $57.53 million.
E-commerce led sectors with $182.69 million, then AI ($131.12 million) and healthtech ($104.61 million). Series B led by stage with $209.34 million across 10 deals.
Exits: Marico bought Satya Nutraceuticals for $110 million. Burma Burma's operator filed for an IPO with a fresh issue of up to Rs 600 crore. Jio Platforms, Zetwerk and AceVector (Snapdeal) listed.
Startups have raised nearly $11 billion in 2026. __If the last two months average $1 billion, the year passes 2023's $13 billion; otherwise 2026 is the lowest in three years__.
signal: Without $100 million-plus rounds, totals swing on a few deals; one or two big cheques in November or December decide whether 2026 beats 2023.
Listings and IPO filings are giving investors exits, which matters more to future fund-raising than any single month's total.
lead.editors_read: The fall is mostly the absence of mega-rounds, not of deals: October still had 108 disclosed deals. Investors are paying for unit economics and profitability, and exits through IPOs and M&A are the way capital gets recycled. If the pattern holds, founders raising now face tougher diligence and smaller cheques, and operators who can show cash discipline have the edge.

frontpage.headline: TRAI drafts AI rules for telecom operators
frontpage.hook: TRAI has published draft guidelines requiring telecom operators to govern, risk-classify and take responsibility for AI systems in their networks, with ==comments open until 27 November 2026==.
points: The draft applies to authorised entities that provide telecom services or run networks and use, or plan to use, AI.
Operators must set internal AI policies, classify AI systems by risk, add human oversight, and run validation and impact assessments before deploying or changing a system.
Critical and high-severity AI incidents must be recorded, investigated and reported to TRAI. Operators must also form an AI Governance and Safety Committee and handle consumer complaints about AI.
Operators stay accountable for outcomes even when the AI is built or supplied by third parties.
It adapts India's broader AI Governance Guidelines of February 2026 to telecom, where AI failures could hit connectivity and essential services.
signal: Because liability stays with the operator, vendors selling AI to telcos will face contract and audit demands from their customers.
If the draft is finalised as written, compliance and AI-governance roles at operators become mandatory.
frontpage.editors_read: Putting liability on the operator, not the AI vendor, is the key design choice. It pushes risk-assessment work down the supply chain. Expect operators to ask suppliers for documentation and indemnities, and expect lobbying on what counts as high severity.

frontpage.headline: Pixxel says it is Indian-owned after backlash over US subsidiary
frontpage.hook: Pixxel CEO Awais Ahmed says the spacetech startup is ==Indian-headquartered, owned and controlled== after criticism of its new US arm, Pixxel Federal.
points: Pixxel Federal will pursue US civilian, defence and intelligence contracts, with an office planned near Washington, DC. Pixxel already works with NASA and the National Reconnaissance Office.
Ahmed says the Indian entity, incorporated in 2018, is not a subsidiary of a US company and runs Pixxel's Indian government, space and defence work. Pixxel Federal's board has no control over it.
Indian investors, including the founders, hold the largest share, followed by investors from Singapore, the UK and the US. No foreign investor has unilateral control, he says.
Rival GalaxEye, without naming Pixxel, said it chose a single Indian entity for all contracts and bids.
Pixxel raised $100 million in a Series C in September, taking total funding to about $195 million. It plans an Indian IPO in a few years, when its full structure would be disclosed.
signal: Multi-country entities are normal in space and defence, but government customers weigh ownership closely; disclosure at IPO will settle the question.
frontpage.editors_read: The row is about trust in defence procurement, where buyers care who controls IP and data. Pixxel's stated firewall between Indian and US entities is the test. A public IPO filing would be the first independent check of these claims.

frontpage.headline: FDA tentatively approves Dr. Reddy's generic HIV prevention injection
frontpage.hook: The FDA gave tentative approval to Dr. Reddy's to make generic lenacapavir, an HIV prevention shot priced at ==$40 per person per year==, with shipping planned next month.
points: Lenacapavir is injected once every six months and offers virtually complete protection against HIV, per the report. Gilead sells the brand version, Yetzugo, approved by the FDA last year.
The $40 annual cost is comparable to daily tablets.
Separately today, Dr. Reddy's told exchanges the approval opens access across 120 countries outside the US under an existing voluntary licence.
signal: Cheap generics under licence let global health groups buy at scale for low- and middle-income countries.
For Indian generics makers, this shows the licence-and-approval route to large public-health volumes.
frontpage.editors_read: The price matches daily pills, which removes cost as the main barrier. Delivery becomes the constraint: clinics, supply chains and funders. Dr. Reddy's gains volume and reputation, though per-unit margins look thin at $40.

frontpage.headline: Cohere seeks up to C$7 billion in Series E at C$35.7 billion valuation
frontpage.hook: Cohere announced an initial close of a ==Series E targeting up to C$7 billion at a C$35.7 billion valuation==, the largest private round by a Canadian tech company.
points: Schwarz Group's companies lead. New investors include Bell Ventures, Bullhound Capital and the Government of Canada; Inovia, NVIDIA and Prosperity7 return.
Cohere says it ended Q3 2026 with 165% year-on-year growth in annual recurring revenue (ARR), driven by its North agentic AI platform.
Customers grew 20x in a year to 300, including RBC, TD Bank, Bell Canada and Fujitsu.
Funds go to models, industry-specific AI products for regulated sectors, and long-term compute for training frontier enterprise models.
Schwarz says it follows Cohere's business combination with Aleph Alpha, and aims to anchor the technology in its STACKIT sovereign cloud.
signal: Government equity and a European cloud lead show buyers paying for control over data and deployment, not just model quality.
frontpage.editors_read: Cohere is selling control and compliance to banks and governments rather than competing on frontier benchmarks. That niche is real if regulators keep demanding data residency. The risk is compute cost: training frontier models needs far more capital than C$7 billion buys over time.

frontpage.headline: India's emissions growth slowed in 2025 as renewables began displacing coal
frontpage.hook: India's renewable power rose 98 TWh in 2025, nearly twice the 49 TWh rise in demand, while ==coal generation fell 44 TWh==, UNEP's Emissions Gap Report says.
points: Datasets disagree on direction: EDGAR and the IEA show a slight decline, the Energy Institute a marginal rise. CREA puts fossil CO2 growth at 0.7%, the slowest since 2001 outside 2020.
Solar added 53 TWh (37%), wind 22 TWh and hydro 21 TWh. Demand grew 2.4% against 6.2% in 2024. Coal's share fell from about 75% to 71%.
Weather helped: a milder summer cut demand by about 32 TWh versus expectation. CREA credits 44% of the reversal to clean power, 36% to lower cooling demand, 20% to slower underlying demand growth.
Steel output rose about 8% and cement about 10%, partly offsetting power-sector cuts. Coal generation is still 46% above 2015.
India emitted about 4.5 billion tonnes CO2e, with 3.1 tonnes per person against a global 6.4. Researchers say storage, transmission and time-of-day tariffs are needed to keep the shift.
signal: If storage and transmission lag, coal fills evening gaps and the 2025 gain fades once hot weather returns.
Demand growth from industry and cooling means clean capacity must keep outpacing it.
frontpage.key_stat: 98 TWh · renewable rise vs 49 TWh demand rise
frontpage.editors_read: One year with favourable weather is not a trend, and researchers say so. The durable part is solar's scale. The investment gap now sits in batteries, grids and industrial decarbonisation.

frontpage.headline: Stocks in focus: GRSE's Rs 32,000 crore Navy contract, Dr Reddy's, HPCL fire
frontpage.hook: Garden Reach Shipbuilders signed a ==Rs 32,000 crore contract with the Indian Navy for five Next Generation Corvettes==, topping today's stock news.
points: GRSE was the lowest bidder and is already building nine warships, including a Project 17A frigate.
Dr Reddy's got US FDA tentative approval for twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir for HIV prevention. Lupin got FDA approval for Amifampridine 10 mg tablets.
HPCL says a fire at a pitch storage tank at its Visakhapatnam refinery around 10 pm on 2 November is controlled, with no damage to units.
NBCC won work orders of about Rs 70.50 crore from Oil India and HAL. Panache DigiLife won a Rs 51.43 crore laptop order due within about 30 days.

Datakosa got a $2.47 million (about Rs 23.38 crore) AI automation order from US-based Hermes Networks, to run for 12 months. Belrise signed a licence with Japan's Yamato for filters and intake manifolds.
signal: The GRSE order extends its order book for years, but execution on a full yard already carrying nine ships is the test.

frontpage.headline: China to restrict tunnel-boring machine exports, hitting India's Himalayan projects
frontpage.hook: China will tighten exports of construction equipment, including tunnel-boring machines, from later this month, and China makes about ==70% of the world's tunnel-boring machines==.
points: Beijing cites dual military and civilian use and says 'sensitive countries and regions with disputes with China' face stricter rules. Components are covered, so maintenance of machines already in use is at risk.
India is a major buyer and is building roads and railways along the disputed Himalayan border. In 2024, China delayed Herrenknecht's sale of such machines to India.

India is weighing a $1.2 billion incentive scheme for domestic makers, expected to draw about $1.8 billion in investment over seven years. L&T is building a prototype, but warns Chinese scale gives it a price edge.
Gadkari aims to invest up to $9.6 billion in tunnelling over five years. Western and Japanese makers exist but switching quickly is hard.
signal: If spare parts are held back, existing machines stall first; India can shift machines between priority projects only briefly.
Bloomberg Economics says tighter controls could push foreign makers to add capacity in India.
frontpage.key_stat: ~70% · China's share of global TBM market
frontpage.editors_read: This is leverage by chokepoint: the part supply matters more than new machines. India's scheme needs prices to compete with China's, or buyers will keep importing. Separately today, the NYT reports Beijing is also moving to control exports of drones, AI models and solar-making processes.

frontpage.headline: Explosions on Iran's Qeshm Island as US reports 'defensive strikes' in Hormuz
frontpage.hook: Five explosions hit Iran's Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz after Iran claimed to down three US drones, and US officials said they carried out ==defensive strikes==.
points: The IRGC says it brought down a US MQ-9 east of Hormuz and captured two MQM-170 reconnaissance drones south of Qeshm. US officials say the strikes hit Iranian surface-to-air missile sites after the IRGC fired at a US aircraft.
A US official says this is not the start of expanded strikes. Trump says he is not considering striking after Tuesday's US midterms.
Iran says its plan to reopen Hormuz could be carried out in two days if the US lifts its naval blockade of Iranian ports and ends hostilities.
Trump claims oil is down almost $10 a barrel on deal hopes. Iran's foreign minister says Tehran is ready for diplomacy or confrontation.
signal: If talks hold, reopening Hormuz would lower oil prices, which matters to India as a large crude importer.
Neither side has confirmed damage or casualties, so claims remain unverified.

stories.headline: India is ChatGPT's largest market; Rapido's order value quadruples
stories.hook: India has become ChatGPT's largest market by weekly active users, with its user base doubling since January, says OpenAI India's managing director.
points: OpenAI says enterprises are moving from pilots to production-scale deployment. It expects UPI and payments announcements in the coming weeks.
Rapido's annualised gross order value (GOV) passed $4 billion, four times two years ago, after a $240 million raise in May at a $3 billion valuation.
Rapido handles about 8.3 million daily orders, over 95% rides, across nearly 500 cities, with an estimated 60% share of bikes, autos and cabs.
Fireside Ventures cofounder Vinay Singh is leaving after nearly a decade to explore agentic commerce.
The government is considering enforcement powers for Cert-In, India's cybersecurity agency, after a rise in AI-driven cyberattacks.
signal: If UPI payments inside ChatGPT launch, it moves from an assistant to a purchase channel in India.

stories.headline: Trajectory raises $45M so nontechnical experts can train AI models
stories.hook: Trajectory, an 18-person startup, raised $45 million in a Series A at a $300 million valuation, led by Sequoia, to automate retraining of AI models.
points: Models don't learn from mistakes without further training. Firms usually fine-tune with in-house research teams or costly forward-deployed engineers.
Trajectory lets companies start from an open-source model, collect feedback from their apps and retrain it, so lawyers or doctors can improve it themselves.
Harvey, Rogo, Decagon, Mercor and Nvidia are customers. The platform is now publicly available.
Rivals include Thinking Machines Lab's Tinker, Applied Compute (valued at $3.25 billion last month) and Prime Intellect.
signal: If specialists can tune models without engineers, the consulting-heavy part of enterprise AI shrinks.

stories.headline: Intel joins $700 million round for AI startup Hark
stories.hook: Intel joined a $700 million funding round for AI startup Hark, alongside Nvidia and AMD Ventures.
points: Hark is building AI-native hardware and digital assistant foundation models that need heavy computing.
The report reads Intel Capital's role as seeding potential customers for Intel's server CPUs, packaging and foundry output.
The risk is Intel's heavy 2026-27 capital spending on US fabs and foundry losses; without disclosed design wins or higher utilisation, the bet looks stretched.
signal: If Hark names Intel chips or foundry in its products, the investment turns into demand; if not, it is just a financial stake.

stories.headline: North Korea denies role in $6.3 billion Binance hack
stories.hook: North Korea called the FBI's claim that it stole more than $6 billion from Binance ==absurd rhetoric==, as TRM Labs counts $6.36 billion taken in about 20 minutes on 29 October.
points: The FBI blames TraderTraitor, the group also tied to the $1.5 billion Bybit theft in February 2025. Trump said 'we don't know if it's North Korea'.
Binance froze about $3 billion, says it has replaced about 90-95% of stolen assets, and will cover all losses. Customers withdrew over $3.6 billion on reopening.
Hackers are converting funds mainly into Ethereum. The FBI asks exchanges to block linked addresses, but cash-out brokers and banks in China sit beyond its reach.
Initial cause was an engineer's compromised laptop; Binance later found more breach points.
signal: Blocking works only where the receiving firm cooperates, so recovery of the rest of the funds looks unlikely.

also.line: Anthropic's quarterly revenue hit nearly $17 billion, twelve times a year earlier, but operating costs of $17.5 billion and a $23.3 billion net loss (from $12.1 billion) preceded its IPO.

Palantir forecast Q4 revenue of about $2.65 billion versus the $2.46 billion estimate after Q3 revenue rose 96% to $2.31 billion; shares fell about 3% as US commercial contract value growth slowed to 11%.

stories.headline: Late-stage funding for Indian startups has fallen sharply from its 2021 peak
stories.hook: Late-stage funding in India fell from a $29.7 billion peak in 2021 to $6.1 billion in 2025 and $5.7 billion by 26 October 2026, per Tracxn.
points: Late-stage rounds dropped from 277 in 2021 to 164 in 2025 and 98 so far in 2026. Angel funding fell from $542 million in 2020 to $95.4 million in 2025.
Investors now price off public-market comparables, wanting positive unit economics and a path to profit. Rupee weakness and US competition for AI capital add pressure.
Tiger Global made 55 Indian investments in 2021 and one in 2026; SoftBank made two in 2026.
Sebi's accredited-investor rules for angel funds had a deadline of 8 September 2026, now extended to 31 March 2027.
One investor expects late-stage funding to pick up around 2028 as AI and deeptech firms mature.
signal: Fund managers face a hard LP fundraising market, so early-stage cheques may shrink before late-stage recovers.

stories.headline: Clinics On Cloud raises Rs 120 crore for its health ATMs
stories.hook: Pune-based Clinics On Cloud raised Rs 120 crore (about $12.5 million) in a Series A from Model42 at a Rs 600 crore valuation, its first institutional funding.
points: It makes AI-enabled health ATMs (self-service kiosks for preventive checks), box clinics and mobile units. The company claims over 3,500 deployments and 12 million screenings across 200 Indian cities and other countries.
Clients include the Army, Navy and BSF, plus corporates such as Reliance and Tata Power.
Funds go to AI, R&D, manufacturing, regulatory compliance and expansion, with the UAE as hub for Africa, the US and Southeast Asia.
The company was founded in 2018 and ran for eight years without outside capital.
signal: A bootstrapped hardware firm with government and defence buyers is now raising to export.
stories.key_stat: Rs 120 Cr · Series A at Rs 600 Cr

stories.headline: Startups edit Chinese open AI models for Western firms
stories.hook: Startups such as Hirundo and Lazarus AI are editing Chinese open-weight models to strip censorship and security flaws, as top Chinese models trail US closed ones by ==just 3% on benchmarks==.
points: Chinese models from DeepSeek, Alibaba and others win on cost and capability and lead Hugging Face downloads. Airbnb, Uber and Harvey have built on them.
CrowdStrike found DeepSeek R1 gave code with severe security flaws up to 50% more often on politically sensitive prompts.
Hirundo edits model weights; Lazarus AI says its realigned Qwen models run at about a dozen US companies.
Some experts say no model can be made universally 'safe'; others say most users do not care about alignment.
signal: Demand comes mainly from regulated buyers; for others, cost still wins.
stories.key_stat: 3% · benchmark gap to US closed models

also.line: Wealthtech PowerUp Money raised $10 million led by Flourish Ventures, with Peak XV, Accel and Blume, at a $73 million valuation, to build AI-led wealth advice.

stories.headline: IZI Enterprise wins DRDO order for VANA surveillance drones
stories.hook: Bhopal-based IZI Enterprise won a DRDO Proof & Experimental Establishment order for its indigenous VANA surveillance drone; value and quantity are undisclosed.
points: VANA does aerial photogrammetry, mapping, surveillance, optical and thermal imaging, live video and autonomous waypoint navigation.
IZI will supply two DGCA-certified pilots for the first year to train DRDO staff during the warranty.
Contract value, drone count and delivery timeline were not made public.
signal: Small orders from DRDO establishments are an early route for private drone makers to larger defence contracts.

also.line: IN-SPACe offered Rs 67.15 crore to four more Indian space startups for satellite propulsion and navigation under its Technology Adoption Fund, bringing selected startups to seven (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: Ukrainian pocket receiver lets troops watch Russian drone video feeds
stories.hook: Kyiv startup CODE380's D·Vision SDR receiver, about 10 ounces, picks up unscrambled live camera video from many Russian drones.
points: Because the drones transmit video unencrypted, a unit can see a drone's heading and target before impact.
It weighs under half of rival Ukrainian models and covers channels Russia's Molniya drones began using in June, which most detectors miss.
Risk: digital video could replace analog and blind such receivers. The New York Times reported some Molniyas are AI-guided with Nvidia chips and emit no signals.
signal: If drones go autonomous and silent, signal-based detection loses value.

stories.headline: Empyrean buys Easy-Logic stake to bolster China's chip design software
stories.hook: Empyrean, China's top EDA (chip design software) provider, will buy 50.38% of Easy-Logic for 218.8 million yuan ($33 million).
points: Easy-Logic, founded in 2021, makes logic optimisation tools; Empyrean says nearly 100 digital chip design firms use its products.
EDA is dominated by Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens EDA; US export controls push Beijing to build local alternatives.
Huawei's Tau Scaling Law aims for 1.4-nanometre-equivalent transistor performance by 2031 without blocked advanced lithography, raising demands on EDA tools.
Empyrean says AI tools cut circuit layout time from four weeks to one.
signal: If Huawei's roadmap depends on domestic EDA, these tools become a chokepoint for China's chip effort.

also.line: Warehouse robotics startup Tutor Intelligence raised a $75 million Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz; it says facilities using its robots nearly quadrupled in a year (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: Modi says clean energy investment cushioned India from West Asia crisis
stories.hook: Modi said India has nearly 300 GW of non-fossil capacity, over 50% of the total, and is targeting 500 GW by 2030.
points: He said growth stayed high despite the West Asia crisis, which would have hurt more without a decade of clean energy investment.
More than Rs 15 lakh crore has been invested in the past decade, Rs 6 lakh crore in the last two years; he sees over Rs 20 lakh crore of opportunity by decade-end.
He urged startups to develop rooftop-solar cooking to cut imported gas, and asked farmers to become 'Urjadata' with panels on spare land.
signal: Cooking and farmland solar are new demand areas that could open if policy follows.

stories.headline: Rajasthan to pilot India's first ceramic heat storage solar plant at Bhadla
stories.hook: RRECL approved NTPC's 320-kilowatt pilot concentrated solar plant at Bhadla that stores heat in ceramic modules to generate power after sunset.
points: Stored heat runs air turbines at night, as a possible lower-cost alternative to chemical batteries. The technology is from US-based 247Solar.
Power from the pilot will serve NTPC's own facilities; approval allows feasibility studies, site assessments and structural testing.
Separately, Jaipur Vidyut Vitran and the Global Energy Alliance invited bids for a 250 kW/250 kWh sodium-ion battery pilot in Jaipur.
signal: If the pilot works, India gets a storage option that avoids imported battery materials.

also.line: India's Rayzon Solar will start up a 5.1-GW solar cell facility in December (headline only; no further detail available).

stories.headline: Foreign funds' share of IPO anchor books hits five-year low
stories.hook: Foreign investors' share of IPO anchor books fell to ==36.16% this year, a five-year low==, from 62.75% in 2021, as domestic institutions fill the gap.
points: Of 104 IPOs raising ₹1.55 trillion in 2026, anchors put in ₹49,771 crore, and FPIs only ₹17,998 crore.
FPIs cite rich valuations, weak listings and a global tilt to AI. They are net sellers in secondary markets, with ₹2.95 trillion out in 2026, while the Nifty 50 is down about 12%.
Mutual funds and insurers are growing: mutual fund assets rose 9.3% to ₹82.64 trillion and monthly SIPs rose 10.7% to ₹32,490 crore in September.
PRIME Database says domestic dominance has scaled back IPO valuations. The Jio Platforms anchor book drew over $25 billion in bids, more than 30 times the shares on offer.
signal: Cheaper IPO pricing helps buyers but trims what founders and sellers raise.

stories.headline: Reuters column: AI selloff raises recession fears
stories.hook: A Reuters column warns an AI-driven selloff could deepen a global slowdown, with the Nasdaq down 10% from its peak and the S&P 500 down 4%.
points: Oxford Economics estimates AI added 0.2 percentage point to GDP growth in six advanced economies in 2025-26, and about a third of US growth of 2.4%.
Stocks are almost 47% of US households' financial assets, a record. Goldman estimates the AI wealth effect added 0.4 percentage point to US consumer spending growth.
Headwinds include Brent at a six-month high, European gas at a four-year high and US mortgage rates above 7%.
The author sees a total AI capex bust as unlikely (summary from limited source text).
signal: If the selloff deepens, spending that rested on stock gains is first to weaken.

also.line: Mainboard IPO fundraising rose 30% to ₹84,400 crore in H1 of this fiscal, with 94% raised between July and September, per Grant Thornton Bharat.

stories.headline: China widens export controls beyond rare earths
stories.hook: In the past month Beijing moved to control exports of dozens of technologies, including drones, AI models and agents, drug-making processes and solar manufacturing methods.
points: Tunnel-boring machines, made mostly in China, are included; the NYT says Beijing is likely to control India's access to them starting next month.
The push could make it harder for US and other firms to set up solar equipment factories to compete with Chinese makers, and harder to access the latest Chinese AI models.
Beijing is doubling down on making Chinese factories indispensable as other governments try to cut reliance on China (limited text available).
signal: Countries with domestic ambitions in solar, drones or pharma face supply constraints they cannot quickly replace.

also.line: India's October diesel demand jumped about 12% year on year, or 214,000 barrels a day, on El Nino dry spells and subsidised fuel prices, per preliminary oil ministry data.
